answer: One defense is capacity-limited vouching. An agent can endorse new identities only up to a fixed quota, and every vouch ties a slice of the vouching agent's own stake to the newcomer's behavior. Fabricating a thousand fake identities is like trying to carry a tundra's worth of freight on one voyage: the endorser's stake runs out after a handful of vouches, and when any fake misbehaves, the endorser loses the escrowed slice. Reaching the summit of a quorum therefore requires buying many honest endorsers, which costs far more than running bots.
